newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity rises in cold temperatures. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT 11/1]
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity rises in cold temperatures. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT 11/1]

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) rose Friday ahead of increased demand expected from cold weather through the weekend and into next week, industry sources said.
Spot sales were said to be relatively thin, with utilities directing most power to firm contract customers during the cold spell, the brokers and marketers said.

Temperatures in northern Texas were expected to reach the mid-20s Fahrenheit Friday with highs in the mid 50s in the south, but were forecast to reach maximums only in the teens in the north of the state on Saturday and in the mid-40s in the south.
From January 14 to 18, temperatures were expected to be much below normal through most of the state.
ERCOT officials said a cold weather advisory was issued for north Texas, requiring utilities in the area to increase their minimum electricity reserve capacity.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Saturday through Monday delivery was talked over a relatively wide range of $36.00-39.00 from next-day discussion at $34.50-36.50 on Thursday.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery for Saturday through Monday's heavy load hours (corrects delivery period) was notationally assessed higher at $34.00-37.00 per MWh, the sources said.

Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Saturday through Monday delivery were pegged at $24.00-27.00 from $19.00-22.00 on Thursday, while non-firm delivery for the same period was pegged at $18.50-21.50 per MWh.
One trader reported hearing offers for 16-hour peak blocks for the five days of next week at $38.00 per MWh.
February ERCOT power was valued higher at $35.50-35.70, although business was said to be thin with few buyers interested in the higher prices. February ERCOT was talked at $33.00-34.00 on Thursday.
Separately, Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 was operating at 100 percent production Friday morning following a weekend shutdown to repair a main feedwater valve.
